_what: Southwestern College's 2026-2027 course descriptions, one row per course the catalog prints (college, subject, code, title, units or hours, requisites, description, source URL, read time). Filed by Sky (S690) under Sam's go of 2026-11-20 (6:26 AM PT, relayed by COBIx on #3584, comment 7042043701), for the M-ID description pipeline and the no-longer-offered catalog factor, which joins on code (the plain session's ask, #3584 comment 7042398748).
fetched_by: Sky (S690), a plain page read under Sam's go of 2026-11-20
how_read: college-page-read.yml on a GitHub runner (index read 44759081085, subjects read 44759854547), through the census Reader: robots.txt first with a plain request that stops at a WAF challenge header (catalog.swccd.edu answered it 200 with content, run 44757980757), 4 s between loads, the user agent naming the CPL Initiative, each subject page printed line for line by the capture view. The runner was served no check and passed none.
parsed_by: A course opens on a line 'SUBJ NNN' (CCN codes such as ARTH C1100 included), then its title, then '<n> UNITS'. The lines up to the next course or 'Back to top' are its grading, requisites (Prerequisite, Corequisite, Recommended Preparation, Recommended Concurrent Enrollment, Advisory, Limitation on Enrollment), the hours line (hours_printed), other labeled lines (Fee, Offered, ...) and its description. The ART page prints its list twice; an identical repeat is kept once (pages[].repeats_dropped).
not_read: Three subject addresses answered 404 and were not retried: /pa/, /rat/ (RA&T) and /tt/ (T&T); their addresses differ from the lower-case code. The programs are the harvest's own read, not this file.

rows.subject: ACCT
rows.title: BASIC BUSINESS BOOKKEEPING
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Recommended Preparation: RDG 158 or equivalent or through the Southwestern College multiple measures placement processes.
rows.description: Introduction to the theory, practice, and methods of bookkeeping with primary emphasis on sole proprietorship and payroll accounting. Emphasis on the complete bookkeeping cycle including the use of special journals, general and subsidiary ledgers, worksheets, and financial statements. [D]

rows.subject: ACCT
rows.title: PAYROLL
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Recommended Preparation: RDG 56 or equivalent or through the Southwestern College multiple measures placement processes.
rows.description: Provides entry-level training in the fundamental skills and knowledge in payroll preparations, such as calculating regular and overtime pay, federal and state tax withholdings, and working with journal entries and financial statement in processing payroll records. [D]

rows.subject: ACCT
rows.title: COMPUTERIZED ACCOUNTING
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Recommended Preparation: RDG 158 or equivalent or through the Southwestern College multiple measures placement processes; ACCT 7 or ACCT 101 or equivalent.
rows.description: Covers the accounting cycle for both service and merchandising businesses using accounting software. [D]

rows.subject: ACCT
rows.title: PRINCIPLES OF ACCOUNTING I
requisites: Recommended Preparation: ACCT 7 or MATH 45 or equivalent or through the Southwestern College multiple measures placement processes; RDG 158 or equivalent or through the Southwestern College multiple measures placement processes.
rows.description: Explore what financial accounting is, why it is important, and how it is used by investors and creditors to make decisions. Covers the recording and reporting of business transactions, the application of generally accepted accounting principles, the classified financial statements, and statement analysis. [D; CSU; UC; C-ID ACCT 110]

rows.subject: ACCT
rows.title: PRINCIPLES OF ACCOUNTING II--- MANAGERIAL
requisites: Recommended Preparation: RDG 158 or equivalent or through the Southwestern College multiple measures placement processes.
Prerequisite: ACCT 101 or equivalent.
rows.description: Covers how managers use accounting information in decision-making, planning, directing operations, and controlling. Focuses on cost terms and concepts, cost behavior, cost structure, and cost-volume-profit analysis. Examines profit planning, standard costs, operations and capital budgeting, cost control, and accounting for costs in manufacturing organizations. [D; CSU; UC; C-ID ACCT 120]

rows.subject: ACCT
rows.title: INTERMEDIATE ACCOUNTING
requisites: Recommended Preparation: ACCT 102 or equivalent.
rows.description: Provides a background for accounting practice and the financial accounting aspects for the CPA examination. Applies accounting theory and practice applicable to handling cash; receivables; inventories; investments; property, plant and equipment; liabilities; and stockholders' equity. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ACCT
rows.title: FEDERAL INCOME TAX
requisites: Recommended Preparation: A one- semester introductory bookkeeping or accounting course.
rows.description: Provides theory and practice in the preparation of Federal and California income tax returns for individuals, with limited review of partnerships and corporations. Presents filing requirements, income inclusions and exclusions, capital gains and losses, business and personal deductions, alternate tax methods, tax credit, and installment and deferred payment sales. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ACCT
rows.title: INDEPENDENT STUDY
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Limitation on Enrollment: Eligibility for independent study.
rows.description: Individual study or research in some area of accounting of particular interest to the student and not included in the regular courses of the college. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: AERO
rows.title: BASIC PROFICIENCY FOR REMOTE PILOTS FLIGHT TRAINING
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Recommended Concurrent Enrollment: AERO 108 or equivalent.
rows.description: Prepares students for different aspects of the Airborne Public Safety Association (APSA)'s Basic Proficiency Evaluation for Remote Pilots (BPERP) certification exam. Emphasizes safety, capabilities, and operation competency in order to prepare students to attain the industry-recognized BPERP certification. Utilizes the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) curriculum for drones. [D; CSU] (Same as: NC 326)

rows.subject: AERO
rows.title: ADVANCED AND CONFINED FLIGHT TRAINING FOR REMOTE PILOTS
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Recommended Concurrent Enrollment: AERO 108, FTMA 108, ART 188, NC 328 or equivalent.
Prerequisite: AERO 105 or equivalent.
rows.description: Provides hands-on drone flight training based on the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) curriculum for drones. Includes a review of NIST Levels 1-3 Open Lanes and scorable Scenarios as well as emphasis on Level 4 Obstruct Lanes and Level 5 Confined Lanes. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: AERO
rows.title: REMOTE PILOT GROUND SCHOOL
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
rows.description: Equips students with knowledge about the regulations and procedures governing the safe and legal operation of small remotely operated aircraft systems (sUAS), commonly referred to as "drones." Coincides with the knowledge areas in the Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA's) Part 107 knowledge test for a Remote Pilot Certificate with a sUAS rating, and is intended to prepare students for the FAA written examination required for students to become commercial sUAS pilots. [D; CSU] (Same as: GEOG 107;NC 327)

rows.subject: AERO
rows.title: INTRODUCTION TO DRONE TECHNOLOGY AND APPLICATIONS
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
rows.description: Introduces remotely operated aircraft systems (drones), including applications, safety, maintenance, mission planning, flying, and data acquisition (multispectral images, photos, and videos). [D; CSU] (Same as: GEOG 108;ART 188;FTMA 108;NC 328)

rows.subject: AFRO
rows.title: AFRICAN-AMERICAN HISTORY I
requisites: Recommended Preparation: or equivalent or through the Southwestern College multiple measures placement processes.
rows.description: Emphasizes the study of the African-American experience from African origins to the conclusion of the Civil War. Focuses on the Atlantic slave trade and slavery in the United States. Includes a study of the Constitution of the United States and the responsibilities of American citizenship. (Partially fulfills American Institutions requirement at CSU.) [D; CSU; UC] (Same as: HIST 110)

rows.subject: AFRO
rows.title: AFRICAN-AMERICAN HISTORY II
rows.description: Explores the history of African Americans from the Civil War to the present, emphasizing their cultural, social, and political impact on American history. Includes a study of the United States Constitution, the State Constitution of California, and discrepancies between rights and the experiences of African Americans. (Partially fulfills American Institutions requirement at CSU.) [D; CSU; UC] (Same as: HIST 111)

rows.subject: AFRO
rows.title: INTRODUCTION TO AFRICAN AMERICAN CULTURE
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
rows.description: Introduces the origins and development of African-American culture from its origins in West and Central Africa to its contemporary manifestations in the United States. Emphasizes the critical analysis of the historical, political, cultural and sociological aspects of the African-American experience in the arenas of family, politics, education, religion, and the arts. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: AFRO
rows.title: INDEPENDENT STUDY
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Limitation on Enrollment: Eligibility for independent study.
rows.description: Individual study or research in some area of African-American studies of particular interest to the student and not included in regular courses of the college. [D; CSU; **UC] (**UC Limitation: credit for variable topics courses is given only after a review of the scope and content of the courses by the enrolling UC campus.)

rows.subject: ASL
rows.title: AMERICAN SIGN LANGUAGE I
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
rows.description: Introduces American Sign Language (ASL) including Fingerspelled signs and numbers utilized in the Deaf community. Provides a basic foundation of language structure, sign recognition, and sign production at the novice level. Introduces students to the historical aspects and origins of ASL and Deaf Culture. Intended for students with no or little knowledge of ASL. Equivalent to two years of high school ASL. [D; CSU; UC] (Formerly: ASL 120)

rows.subject: ASL
rows.title: AMERICAN SIGN LANGUAGE II
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Prerequisite: ASL 101 or equivalent.
rows.description: Provides a continuation to enhance fluency in comprehension skill development and sign production in American Sign Language (ASL). Expands sign vocabulary and complex grammatical structures for carrying out basic interpersonal communication on various topics, such as describing people, places, and plans. Continues the learning of ASL, Deaf culture, Deaf art, Deaf heritage, and customs of the Deaf community. Equivalent to three years of high school ASL. [D; CSU; UC] (Formerly: ASL 130)

rows.subject: ASL
rows.title: AMERICAN SIGN LANGUAGE III
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Prerequisite: ASL 102 or equivalent.
rows.description: Provides an extensive review of all first-year structures. Focuses on interpersonal communication for intermediate students. Covers grammatical structures and vocabulary necessary to discuss personal relations, food, travel, health, environment, and culture. Engages with literary works that delve into Deaf worldviews and critically analyzes ASL literature. Equivalent to four years of high school ASL. [D; CSU; UC] (Formerly: ASL 220)

rows.subject: ASL
rows.title: AMERICAN SIGN LANGUAGE IV
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Prerequisite: ASL 201 or equivalent.
rows.description: Provides continuation of ASL 201. Advances comprehension and production skills in American Sign Language (ASL) to an intermediate-high level, covering various topics such as literature, values, traditions, history, art, politics, and environment. Emphasis is on nuanced linguistic features and cultural insights essential for effective communication within the Deaf community. Emphasizes further study of abstract concepts, specialized vocabulary, and advanced ASL literature analysis, fostering fluency in diverse professional and artistic contexts. Analyzes and appreciates works of historical, literary, and cultural importance in the ASL community. This course corresponds to the fourth year of high school ASL. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ASL
rows.title: DEAF CULTURE
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Recommended Preparation: RDG 158 or equivalent or through the Southwestern College multiple measures placement processes.
rows.description: Provides an introduction of Deaf culture where students learn a wide array of historical milestones that shaped the belief system, behavioral norms, and perspectives of members in the Deaf community. Examines the complexity of the ASL structure as well as how other sign systems played a role in the development. Provides further in-depth information about ASL literature, Deaf contributors, social and political influences, and ever-changing technological advancements that form the dynamics and influences within the Deaf culture. [D; CSU; UC] (Formerly: ASL 150)

rows.subject: ASL
rows.title: FINGERSPELLING, NUMBERS, AND DEPICTION IN ASL
requisites: Recommended Concurrent Enrollment: ASL 201.
Prerequisite: ASL 102 or equivalent.
rows.description: Provides a foundational understanding of fingerspelling, number use, and depiction in American Sign Language (ASL), with an emphasis on expressive and receptive accuracy. Explores the historical, linguistic, and physiological aspects of ASL handshapes and their use in conveying detailed visual information. Develops skills in recognizing and producing fingerspelled words, number sequences, and descriptive classifiers through appropriate biomechanical functions and spatial awareness. Emphasizes visual tracking, clarity, and depicting techniques to support natural and effective communication in ASL. Recommended for students concurrently enrolled in ASL 201 to strengthen overall fluency and precision. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ASL
rows.title: INDEPENDENT STUDY
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Limitation on Enrollment: Eligibility for independent study.
rows.description: Individual study or research in some area of American sign language of particular interest to the student and not included in regular courses of the college. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ANTH
rows.title: BIOLOGICAL ANTHROPOLOGY
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Recommended Preparation: RDG 158 or equivalent or through the Southwestern College multiple measures placement processes.
rows.description: Introduces a natural history of humankind and scientific evidence for human evolution. Includes the study of genetics and heredity, taxonomy, the study of primates, evolutionary theory, and modern population adaptations and variation. Emphasizes skeletal analysis and the evaluation of the hominid fossil record. [D; CSU; UC; C-ID ANTH 110]

rows.subject: ANTH
rows.title: LABORATORY IN BIOLOGICAL ANTHROPOLOGY
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Corequisite: ANTH 101 (may be taken previously).
rows.description: Provides a practical study of biological anthropology. Explores field and laboratory studies in genetics, human variation, human osteology, anthropometry, hominid/hominin evolution, comparative primate anatomy, primate behavior, and forensic anthropology. Intended for anthropology majors and all students interested in life and/or behavioral sciences. [D; CSU; UC; C-ID ANTH 115L]

rows.subject: ANTH
rows.title: CULTURAL ANTHROPOLOGY
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Recommended Preparation: RDG 158 or equivalent or through the Southwestern College multiple measures placement processes.
rows.description: Introduces the social and cultural adaptations of various peoples around the world to geographic, historical, and socioeconomic conditions. Focuses on comparative systems of communications, economics, family/kingship, government, and religion. [D; CSU; UC; C-ID ANTH 120]

rows.subject: ANTH
rows.title: ARCHAEOLOGY AND PREHISTORY
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Recommended Preparation: RDG 158 or equivalent or through the Southwestern College multiple measures placement processes.
rows.description: Introduces the fundamentals of the history, methods, and theoretical approaches of archaeology and its application to the study of ancient civilizations. Emphasizes the techniques of data collection and analysis, cultural reconstruction and interpretation, and cultural resource management work. Uses a globally comparative case-study approach. [D; CSU; UC; C-ID ANTH 150]

rows.subject: ANTH
rows.title: CULTURES OF MEXICO
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Recommended Preparation: RDG 158 or equivalent or through the Southwestern College multiple measures placement processes.
rows.description: Explores the culture history of indigenous societies in the zone known anthropologically as Mesoamerica. Focuses on the unique character of selected cultures, including ecological adaptations and major technological and cultural innovations. Explores the impact of Old World cultural and biological elements in creation of the region's modern society. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ANTH
rows.title: MAGIC, RELIGION, WITCHCRAFT, AND HEALING
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
rows.description: Explores cross-cultural perspectives on spirituality, magic, religious beliefs, health/healing, and diversity of globally found religious and/or ritual practitioners who construct emotional, spiritual, physical health, and well-being. Emphasizes the understanding of cosmologies, religious practices, and beliefs of others assists in understanding the modern multi-cultural world. Assesses cultural perspectives concerning human existence, relationship to universe, meaning of life, health, birth, and death. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ANTH
rows.title: INDEPENDENT STUDY
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Limitation on Enrollment: Eligibility for independent study.
rows.description: Individual study or research in some area of Anthropology of particular interest to the student and not included in regular courses of the college. [D; CSU; **UC] (**UC Limitation: credit for variable topics courses is given only after a review of the scope and content of the courses by the enrolling UC campus.

rows.subject: ARCH
rows.title: INTRODUCTION TO ARCHITECTURE AND ENVIRONMENTAL DESIGN
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Recommended Concurrent Enrollment: ARCH 110, ANTH 112, ARCH 115, or ARCH 150.
rows.description: Develops an understanding of the built environment. Explores architectural design, history, theory, and practice. Provides an overview of architectural representation, model-making techniques, and design psychology. Includes the study of urban planning and interior design. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ARCH
rows.title: FREEHAND DRAWING FOR DESIGNERS
rows.description: Introduces drawing in media including, but not limited to, graphite pencil, felt marker, and ink. Provides a study of drawing fundamentals, sketching, and presentation drawings from elements found in the built environment and from nature. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ARCH
rows.title: ARCHITECTURAL RENDERING
rows.description: Explores the theory and practice of the development of architectural renderings. Studies and practices the use of various media and techniques involved. Provides an approach to drawing in color in order to efficiently and effectively illustrate design ideas. Introduces the use of digital media as an architectural visualization tool. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ARCH
rows.title: ADVANCED ARCHITECTURAL RENDERING
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Recommended Preparation: ARCH 112 or equivalent.
rows.description: Advanced rendering techniques using color marker, color pencil, and exploration of other medium. Portfolio preparation. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ARCH
rows.title: GRAPHIC COMMUNICATION FOR ARCHITECTS AND DESIGNERS
rows.description: Explores the fundamental technical aspects and basic theories of architectural graphic representation. Includes the study of orthographic and axonometric projection, perspective drawing, shade, shadow, tonal value, diagramming, typography and architectural presentation development through various media and techniques. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ARCH
rows.title: PORTFOLIO DEVELOPMENT FOR ARCHITECTS AND DESIGNERS
requisites: Recommended Preparation: ARCH 115 or ARCH 150 or equivalent.
Recommended Concurrent Enrollment: ARCH 252 and ARCH 253 (may be taken previously).
rows.description: Establishes an understanding of the process of developing, designing, and assembling a portfolio of creative work. Studies techniques of: curation, visual structure, organizational strategies, representational strategies, editing, text, and delivery methods as related to an architectural or design portfolio. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ARCH
rows.title: ARCHITECTURAL DESIGN I
rows.description: Introduces the theories and principles of architectural design and the development of problem solving skills as related to three-dimensional spatial design problems. Emphasizes drawing and modeling as a means to design. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ARCH
rows.title: ARCHITECTURAL DESIGN II
requisites: Prerequisite: ARCH 150 or equivalent.
Corequisite: ARCH 165 (may be taken previously).
rows.description: Explores theories and principles of design as applied to the development of architectural space. Analyzes architectural form through three-dimensional modeling. Studies methods and problem-solving strategies with application to architectural design. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ARCH
rows.title: ARCHITECTURAL PRACTICE I
requisites: Recommended Preparation: RDG 158 or equivalent or through the Southwestern College multiple measures placement processes.
rows.description: Introduces principles of building construction and technology. Provides an overview of the major systems of a building. Includes construction document preparation, architectural drafting, and detailing. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ARCH
rows.title: INTRODUCTION TO COMPUTER AIDED DESIGN
requisites: Recommended Preparation: ARCH 150 or equivalent.
rows.description: Introduces computer aided design as applied to the architectural field - using AutoCAD. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ARCH
rows.title: BEGINNING BUILDING INFORMATION MODELING
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Recommended Preparation: ARCH 165 or equivalent; RDG 158 or equivalent or through the Southwestern College multiple measures placement processes.
rows.description: Introduces Building Information Modeling (BIM), an integrated process built on coordinated information for architectural projects. Improves drawing coordination, enhances accuracy, reduces waste, and enables better-informed decisions. Develops skills in the architectural field using Revit Architecture building information modeling software. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ARCH
rows.title: ADVANCED BUILDING INFORMATION MODELING
requisites: Prerequisite: ARCH 201 or equivalent.
rows.description: Continues the study of ARCH 201. Develops advanced skills in the use of AutoDesk's Revit Architecture as applied to architectural design best office practices. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ARCH
rows.title: ADVANCED ARCHITECTURAL CAD
requisites: Prerequisite: ARCH 200 or equivalent.
rows.description: Continues the study of ARCH 200 for students who wish to develop advanced CAD skills as applied to the architectural field using AutoCAD. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ARCH
rows.title: WORLD ARCHITECTURE I
requisites: Recommended Preparation: RDG 158 or equivalent or through the Southwestern College multiple measures placement processes.
rows.description: Studies the formal, cultural, aesthetic, and sociopolitical dimensions of architecture from prehistory to the beginning of the Industrial Revolution in the 1750s. Provides an understanding of the influences and the forces that most critically impact the design and building practices of past cultures and societies. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ARCH
rows.title: CONSTRUCTION SURVEYING
rows.description: Basic surveying as related directly to building construction. Use of the standard surveying instruments in the measuring and laying out of buildings, topographic surveying, and the establishing of levels and profiles. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ARCH
rows.title: WORLD ARCHITECTURE II
requisites: Recommended Preparation: RDG 158 or equivalent or through the Southwestern College multiple measures placement processes.
rows.description: Studies the formal, cultural, aesthetic, and sociopolitical dimensions of architecture from the mid-eighteenth century to the present day. Provides an understanding of the influences and the forces that most critically impact the design and building practices of both the past and the present. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ARCH
rows.title: ENVIRONMENTAL CONTROLS
requisites: Recommended Preparation: RDG 158 or equivalent or through the Southwestern College multiple measures placement processes.
rows.description: Introduces the physical relationship between man and his environment. Studies the physical phenomena (heat, light, and sound) as it relates to our existence and comfort. Introduces fundamentals of climate-responsive design of the built environment and study of Green Building Codes. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ARCH
rows.title: STRUCTURES
requisites: Recommended Preparation: RDG 158 or equivalent or through the Southwestern College multiple measures placement processes; MATH 62 or MATH 72 or equivalent or through the Southwestern College multiple measures placement processes.
rows.description: Analyzes forces on building structures. Studies static equilibrium, shear, bending moment diagrams, stress and strain relationships, and deformation in structures. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ARCH
rows.title: ARCHITECTURAL DESIGN III
requisites: Prerequisite: ARCH 151 or equivalent.
Corequisite: ARCH 265.
rows.description: Continues the study of the principles of architectural design. Studies analysis techniques as applied to space adjacency, contextual issues of architectural design, and the meaning of architectural form. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ARCH
rows.title: ARCHITECTURAL DESIGN IV
requisites: Prerequisite: ARCH 252 or equivalent.
Corequisite: ARCH 266.
rows.description: Continues the study of the principles of architectural design. Applies design techniques and strategies to the solution of an architectural design problem. Integrates building code requirements to an architectural solution. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ARCH
rows.title: ARCHITECTURAL PRACTICE II
requisites: Prerequisite: ARCH 165 or equivalent.
rows.description: Studies the processes of building from design through construction. Explores the application of building/green codes and standards to the design and construction of a building. Includes a study of building nomenclature, construction technology, and structural components. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ARCH
rows.title: ARCHITECTURAL PRACTICE III
requisites: Prerequisite: ARCH 265 or equivalent.
rows.description: Continues the study of ARCH 265. Explores building construction processes including the study of thermal and moisture protection, mechanical, electrical, and plumbing building systems. Applies building/green codes and standards to building construction. Studies construction documents, AIA contracts, and construction management with application of the critical path method. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ARCH
rows.title: ARCHITECTURE LABORATORY
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Recommended Preparation: RDG 158 or equivalent or through the Southwestern College multiple measures placement processes.
rows.description: Provides a supplemental laboratory to the architecture design studios and practice courses. Covers the safe use of hand and power tools used in the model shop. Includes the application of design principles and problem solving scenarios to directed projects and presentation strategies as applied to directed projects. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ARCH
rows.title: INDEPENDENT STUDY
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Limitation on Enrollment: Eligibility for independent study.
rows.description: Individual study or research in some area of architecture of particular interest to the student and not included in regular courses of the college. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: BASIC SCREEN PRINTING
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
rows.description: Introduces students to the theory and applications of silk-screen printing methods and techniques with emphasis on paper stencil, drawing fluid and photo emulsion on diverse surfaces. [ND]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: INTERMEDIATE SCREEN PRINTING
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Recommended Preparation: ART 100 or equivalent.
Recommended Concurrent Enrollment: ART 116 or ART 117.
Prerequisite: ART 14 or equivalent.
rows.description: Provides advanced theory and applications of silk-screen printing methods and techniques. Allows an in-depth understanding of image reproduction from artistic to industrial processes. [ND]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: DRAWING I
requisites: Recommended Concurrent Enrollment: ART 101.
rows.description: Introduces materials, methods, and conceptual approaches to drawing. Emphasizes principles of contrast, perspective, movement, texture, and value combined with training in the use of diverse materials and offers a practical as well as theoretical appreciation for drawing. [D; CSU; UC; C-ID ARTS 110]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: DRAWING LABORATORY I
requisites: Corequisite: ART 100.
rows.description: Intended to substantiate the skill development for student portfolios and encourage the use of materials, methods, creative thinking, and problem solving introduced to the student in the ART 100. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: DESIGN I
rows.description: Introduces two-dimensional arts through the study of cultural, historical, and theoretical perspectives on aesthetics and creative expression. Examines form and content through creative investigation of the elements and principles of design. Applies specialized vocabulary and theories of perception in the description and analysis of works of art. [D; CSU; UC; C-ID ARTS 100]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: DRAWING II
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 100 or equivalent.
rows.description: Continues the expansion of drawing concepts introduced in ART 100. [D; CSU; UC; C-ID ARTS 205]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: DRAWING LABORATORY II
rows.description: Develops skills for the creation of student portfolio and encourages the use of materials, methods, creative thinking, and problem solving introduced to the student in ART 102. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: DESIGN II
requisites: Recommended Preparation: ART 101 or equivalent.
rows.description: Introduces the study of elements and principles of three-dimensional design, its functional application in art and society, the history of design, and the philosophies that influence the use of the three-dimensional space. Emphasizes the analysis of human perception, aesthetics theory, and critical judgment through the development of volumetric forms. [D; CSU; UC; C-ID ARTS 101]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: OPEN STUDIO: THREE-DIMENSIONAL MEDIA LAB/DESIGN II
requisites: Corequisite: ART 103.
rows.description: Provides a lab course designed to augment comprehension of the principles of design and the application of appropriate utilization of tools and machinery in completing three-dimensional art projects assigned in ART 103. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: INTRODUCTION TO ART
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
rows.description: Provides a general introduction to visual arts that includes the study of theory, terminology, themes, design principles, media, techniques, interpretation, and evaluation of works of art across time and diverse cultures. Introduces skills needed for analysis of historical art context including defining and differentiating functions and methodologies of art history and art criticism. [D; CSU; UC; C-ID ARTH 100]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: LIFE DRAWING I
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 100 or equivalent.
rows.description: Emphasizes the application of gesture, proportion, balance, sighting, value, and perspective in drawing the human figure accurately. Includes the application of intellect and imagination to creative interpretation of the human form. [D; CSU; UC; C-ID ARTS 200]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: LIFE DRAWING II
requisites: Recommended Preparation: ART 100 or equivalent.
Prerequisite: ART 105 or equivalent.
rows.description: Emphasizes advanced practices in drawing the live human form in a variety of media. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: PAINTING I
requisites: Recommended Preparation: ART 100 and ART 101, or equivalent.
rows.description: Emphasizes an introduction to material, methods, and conceptual approaches to painting, including the use of digital technologies as a creative tool for painters. Explores the historical and contemporary painting styles. [D; CSU; UC; C-ID ARTS 210]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: PAINTING LABORATORY I
requisites: Corequisite: ART 107.
rows.description: Explores the range of skills required for the development of student portfolios. Encourages the use of materials, methods, creative thinking, and problem solving. [D]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: PAINTING II
requisites: Recommended Preparation: ART 100 and ART 101, or equivalent.
Recommended Concurrent Enrollment: ART 108L.
Prerequisite: ART 107 or equivalent.
rows.description: Explores advanced concepts and ideas in painting. Emphasizes composition, color, and a variety of materials and techniques, including the use of digital technology as a creative tool for artists. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: PAINTING LABORATORY II
requisites: Corequisite: ART 108.
rows.description: Explores advanced concepts and ideas in painting. Emphasizes composition, color, and a variety of materials and techniques, including the use of digital technology as a creative tool for artists. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: SCULPTURE I
requisites: Recommended Preparation: ART 100 or ART 101 or equivalent.
rows.description: Introduces three-dimensional sculpture principles through the use of traditional processes and materials such as clay, plaster, wood, metal, plastic, and assemblage. Incorporates new experimental and contemporary procedures and techniques through personal development of imagery, content, and appropriation of social and human context. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: OPEN STUDIO: THREE-DIMENSIONAL MEDIA LAB/SCULPTURE I
requisites: Corequisite: ART 110.
rows.description: Provides extended instruction, augmenting comprehension of the principles of art and design, and the application of appropriate utilization of tools and machinery in completing three-dimensional projects. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: SCULPTURE II
requisites: Recommended Preparation: ART 100 or ART 101 or equivalent.
Prerequisite: ART 110 or equivalent.
rows.description: Introduces advanced conceptual and creative assimilation of sculptural processes through the use of traditional and non-traditional materials, theoretical perspectives, refinement of personal imagery, and research on the field. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: OPEN STUDIO: THREE-DIMENSIONAL MEDIA LAB/SCULPTURE II
requisites: Corequisite: ART 111.
rows.description: Provides extended instruction, augmenting comprehension of principles of design and the application of appropriate utilization of tools and machinery in completing advanced sculptural projects assigned in ART 111. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: ARTS OF AFRICA, OCEANIA, AND INDIGENOUS NORTH AMERICAS
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
rows.description: Introduces the arts of Sub-Saharan Africa, Oceania, and Indigenous North America with a look at environmental, economic, social, political, religious, and philosophical issues that help to mold the aesthetics and art of small scale societies. Influences of non-Western art on the mainstream Western art world are also covered. [D; CSU; UC; C-ID ARTH 140]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: ART AND CULTURE OF PRE-HISPANIC MEXICO
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
rows.description: Surveys Mesoamerican and Andean art viewed within the context of economic, sociopolitical, religious, and philosophical systems to show how the worldview affected the art aesthetic pre-European contact. Explores the influence of pre-Columbian art on contemporary Mexican artists. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: COLOR THEORY
requisites: Recommended Concurrent Enrollment: ART 107 or ART 108.
rows.description: Investigates and emphasizes the phenomenon of light and color, and their use in art and design. Explores the historical and contemporary theories of color and their application as well as the perceptual, symbolic, and cultural significances. [D; CSU; UC; C-ID ARTS 270]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: PRINTMAKING I
requisites: Recommended Preparation: ART 100 or ART 101 or equivalent.
rows.description: Covers the design and production of original prints utilizing a variety of materials and techniques, including intaglio (etching and drypoint), relief printing (woodcut and linocut), embossing, and basic planographic processes such as monotyping and screen printing. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: OPEN STUDIO - PRINTMAKING LABORATORY I
requisites: Corequisite: ART 116.
rows.description: Provides instruction on augmenting comprehension of printmaking processes and the application of appropriate utilization of tools and equipment in completing print editions. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: PRINTMAKING II
requisites: Recommended Preparation: ART 100 or ART 101 or equivalent.
Prerequisite: ART 116 or equivalent.
rows.description: Studies the traditional and contemporary printmaking processes focusing on personal imagery, conceptual experimentation, and the importance of social context. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: OPEN STUDIO - PRINTMAKING LABORATORY II
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Corequisite: ART 117.
rows.description: Provides instruction on augmentative practice and development of editions for portfolios ranging from traditional printmaking techniques to experimental methods. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: DARKROOM AND DIGITAL PHOTOGRAPHY
requisites: Recommended Concurrent Enrollment: ART 121L.
rows.description: Focuses on photography as a creative art, emphasizing aesthetics, composition, content, and technical aspects of the medium. Introduces camera operation, darkroom techniques, and digital imaging techniques. Student must furnish an adjustable camera. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: ASIAN ART
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
rows.description: Emphasizes an introduction to the art of China, Japan, India, Central Asia, Southeast Asia, and Indonesia from prehistory to the present, viewed within the social, political, religious, and philosophical framework that shapes Eastern aesthetics. Includes influences of Eastern art on Western art. [D; CSU; UC; C-ID ARTH 130]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: HISTORY OF FILM AS ART
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
rows.description: Provides a survey of cinema with an emphasis on the chronological development of styles and techniques in the medium. Focuses on aesthetic and historical influences on cinema as well as the effects of cinema on society. Discusses the impact of television on film and popular culture. [D; CSU; UC] (Formerly: TELE 113; Same as: FTMA 161)

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: INTRODUCTION TO MOTION PICTURE PRODUCTION
requisites: Prerequisite: FTMA 100 or equivalent; FTMA 101 or equivalent.
rows.description: Provides an introduction to the theory, terminology, and process of motion picture production for film, television, and digital media. Includes basic cinematography including the operation, function and creative uses of pre-production, production and post-production, gaffing and grip equipment, scriptwriting, camera operation, camera composition, principles of lighting and lighting techniques, sound recording and sound design, digital graphics, and digital editing. [D; CSU; UC] (Formerly: TELE 131; Same as: FTMA 102)

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: MOTION PICTURE PRODUCTION
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Prerequisite: FTMA 102 or ART 131 or equivalent.
rows.description: Uses digital video as a means of creative expression with an emphasis on directing, cinematography, sound recording, editing and post-production techniques. Includes screenwriting, producing, directing, director of photography, sound mixing and design, and editing. [D; CSU; UC] (Formerly: TELE 132; Same as: FTMA 112)

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: EXPERIMENTAL MEDIA
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
rows.description: Explores and practices nontraditional utilization of media technology and theory in the production of creative work. Encourages interdisciplinary experimentation. [D; CSU; UC] (Same as: FTMA 114)

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: ADVANCED DIGITAL IMAGING FOR PHOTOGRAPHY, ART, AND GRAPHICS
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Recommended Preparation: Advanced skills on Macintosh computers, Adobe Photoshop, and advanced photographic skills.
Recommended Concurrent Enrollment: ART 138L.
Prerequisite: ART 192 or equivalent.
rows.description: Presents advanced techniques in the use of Adobe Photoshop with an emphasis on the production of photographic images. Introduces color calibration, color theory and the use of the zone system for precise control of digital output. Students will apply these concepts to the production of a portfolio of digital photographs. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: ADVANCED DIGITAL IMAGING FOR PHOTOGRAPHY ART AND GRAPHICS LABORATORY
requisites: Corequisite: ART 138.
rows.description: Allows digital imaging students to practice and review techniques and concepts introduced in Advanced Digital Imaging. Provides an opportunity for the student to refine photographic skills beyond normal classroom time. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: AIRBRUSH I
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Recommended Preparation: ART 107 or equivalent.
rows.description: Provides the student of little or no airbrush experience with comprehensive instruction and application of basic airbrush. Emphasizes maintenance and use of the airbrush, reassembly, adjustments, controls, and terminology. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: AIRBRUSH II
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 148A or equivalent.
rows.description: Teaches fundamentals of airbrushing with intermediate demands on bolder compositions and texture synthesis for a deeper understanding of the dynamic airbrush process. Focuses on assigned still-life projects with dramatic lighting, value grouping, and varied color-gradient challenges. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: AIRBRUSH III
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 148B or equivalent.
rows.description: Covers advanced level of airbrushing involving compositional principles of a complex order. Explores stencil management and a wider use of color-gradient combinations. Focuses on planning and completing of an airbrush art piece to reflect the tenets of a particular historical art style interpreted through personal vision. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: AIRBRUSH IV
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 148C or equivalent.
rows.description: Increases the student autonomy in airbrushing at a more demanding pace. Provides techniques to allow additional exploration and mastery of the airbrush. Emphasizes on deeper personal level of connectedness between form and content within a self-directed and challenging environment. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: WOMEN IN WESTERN ART HISTORY, 1550- PRESENT
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
rows.description: Introduces a survey of women artists in Western art from the Renaissance to the present. Emphasizes the emergence of the female artist, including her education, exhibition record, styles, techniques, subject matter, and social circumstances. Includes an examination of the major art periods, theories, criticism, and feminist criticism. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: HISTORY OF PHOTOGRAPHY
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
rows.description: Covers the survey of the history of photography from its invention to its continued use as an art and communication form. Emphasizes the aesthetic and historical influences on photography, as well as photography effects upon society and culture. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: NINETEENTH THROUGH TWENTY-FIRST CENTURY ART
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
rows.description: Introduces modern and contemporary artistic trends and philosophical ideas to enhance students' appreciation of the history of visual cultural production from the nineteenth through twenty-first centuries. Analyzes the aesthetic and cultural development of painting, sculpture, architecture, and handicrafts. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: GRAPHIC DESIGN---LAYOUT
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
rows.description: Teaches elements and principles of design as they relate to publication layout. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: GRAPHIC DESIGN---TYPOGRAPHY
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 159 and ART 161, or equivalent.
rows.description: Covers the creative and practical use of the alphabet in graphic communication. Explores the typographic form through traditional and Macintosh graphics applications. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: GRAPHIC DESIGN
requisites: Recommended Preparation: ART 101 or equivalent.
rows.description: Covers the application of elements and principles of design in development of pictorial symbols, logos, and information graphics. Focuses on vector graphics software. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: GRAPHIC IMAGERY
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 159 and ART 161, or equivalent.
rows.description: 00. Focuses on developing graphic imagery for use in branding, pictorial symbols, and illustration. Includes the development of original graphics and images from concept to completion using vector and imaging software. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: BEGINNING CERAMICS
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
rows.description: Focuses on design and construction of clay forms including an introduction to the use of the potter's wheel. Emphasizes form and its enhancement through a variety of glazing and firing processes. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: INTERMEDIATE CERAMICS
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 170 or equivalent.
rows.description: Emphasizes the further development of skills in ceramic media, emphasizing individual work in vessel and/or sculptural forms. Focuses on construction, scale, surface design, and kiln functions. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: ADVANCED CERAMICS
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 171 or equivalent.
rows.description: Focuses on advanced problems in clay media emphasizing design and further development of individual solutions. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: FIGURATIVE CERAMIC SCULPTURE I
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
rows.description: Includes realistic, expressive, and experimental rendering of the human figure primarily in clay media. Reviews the historical and contemporary role of figurative art. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: FIGURATIVE CERAMIC SCULPTURE II
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 173A or equivalent.
rows.description: Develops continued realistic, expressionistic, and experimental rendering of the human figure primarily in clay and other media. References the historical and contemporary role the figure plays in modern art. Addresses social content, personal vision, and critical thinking as part of project development. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: FIGURATIVE CERAMIC SCULPTURE III
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 173B or equivalent.
rows.description: Continues to advance the three-dimensional study of the human form rendered primarily in clay. Explores traditional instruction regarding the modeling of the figure, installation, and site specific applications. Develops the student's relationship with historical and contemporary sculpture. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: FIGURATIVE CERAMIC SCULPTURE IV
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 173C or equivalent.
rows.description: Continues to further advance the study of the human figure rendered primarily in clay. Investigates traditional as well as contemporary issues as they relate to utilizing the human form in sculpture. Explores installation, site specific, digital imaging, and projection in the execution of assigned projects. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: FUNCTIONAL WHEEL POTTERY I
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 170 or equivalent.
rows.description: Concentrates on the production of functional pottery made primarily on the potter's wheel. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: FUNCTIONAL WHEEL POTTERY II
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 177 or equivalent.
rows.description: Continues development of design and technical skills as applied to functional pottery. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: DESIGN IN WOOD I
rows.description: Explores the use of wood as a utilitarian and artistic medium. Focuses on the history of wood working, design, artistic expression, and joinery techniques. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: OPEN STUDIO: THREE-DIMENSIONAL MEDIA LAB/DESIGN IN WOOD I
requisites: Corequisite: ART 182.
rows.description: Provides extended instruction, augmenting comprehension of the principles of art and design and the application of appropriate utilization of tools and machinery in completing three-dimensional designs in wood. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: DESIGN IN WOOD II
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 182 or equivalent.
rows.description: Explores wood as a creative medium. Continues the development of personal design statement. Offers specialized woodworking and joinery techniques focused on sculptural forms and furniture construction. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: OPEN STUDIO: THREE-DIMENSIONAL MEDIA LAB/DESIGN IN WOOD II
requisites: Corequisite: ART 183.
rows.description: Provides extended instruction, augmenting comprehension of the principles of art and design and the application of appropriate utilization of tools and machinery in completing three-dimensional designs in wood. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: JEWELRY AND METALWORK I
requisites: Recommended Preparation: ART 101 or ART 103 or equivalent.
rows.description: Introduces the fundamentals of design, construction, and fabrication of jewelry and metalwork. Includes physical properties of metals, surface embellishment, soldering, forming, safe use of tools and chemicals, and exposure to historical and contemporary jewelry and metalwork. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: JEWELRY AND METALWORK II
requisites: Recommended Preparation: ART 101 or ART 103 or equivalent.
Prerequisite: ART 185A or equivalent.
rows.description: Covers an intermediate instruction in the design, construction, and fabrication of jewelry and metalwork. Emphasizes the fundamentals of smithing, including sinking, forging, hinge creation, use of hydraulic press, and/or titanium anodizer. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: JEWELRY AND METALWORK III
requisites: Recommended Preparation: ART 101 or ART 103 or equivalent.
Prerequisite: ART 185B or equivalent.
rows.description: Covers an advanced instruction in design, construction, and fabrication of jewelry and metalwork. Introduces the use and properties of precious metals, and a more complex soldering operations and techniques such as raising, anticlastic forming, mechanisms, and stonesetting. Emphasizes the perfecting finishing skills. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: JEWELRY AND METALWORK IV
requisites: Recommended Preparation: ART 101 or ART 103 or equivalent.
Prerequisite: ART 185C or equivalent.
rows.description: Continues advanced instruction in design and construction of jewelry and metalwork. Introduces designing for production and how to price and market work. Emphasizes more self-directed exploration and personal design statements, including alternate processes. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: OPEN STUDIO: THREE-DIMENSIONAL MEDIA LAB/JEWELRY AND METALWORK I
requisites: Corequisite: ART 185A, ART 185B, ART 185C, or ART 185D.
rows.description: Provides extended instruction, augmenting comprehension of the principles of art and design, and the application of appropriate utilization of tools in completing metalwork projects at a beginning level. [D; CSU] (Formerly: ART 185L)

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: OPEN STUDIO: THREE-DIMENSIONAL MEDIA LAB/JEWELRY AND METALWORK II
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 186A or equivalent.
rows.description: Provides extended instruction, augmenting comprehension of the principles of art and design, and the application of appropriate utilization of tools in completing metalwork projects at an intermediate level. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: OPEN STUDIO: THREE-DIMENSIONAL MEDIA LAB/JEWELRY AND METALWORK III
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 186B or equivalent.
rows.description: Provides extended instruction, augmenting comprehension of the principles of art and design, and the application of appropriate utilization of tools in completing metalwork projects at the intermediate-advanced level. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: OPEN STUDIO: THREE-DIMENSIONAL MEDIA LAB/JEWELRY AND METALWORK IV
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 186C or equivalent.
rows.description: Provides extended instruction, augmenting comprehension of the principles of art and design, and the application of appropriate utilization of tools in completing metalwork projects at an advanced level. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: INTRODUCTION TO DRONE TECHNOLOGY AND APPLICATIONS
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
rows.description: Introduces remotely operated aircraft systems (drones), including applications, safety, maintenance, mission planning, flying, and data acquisition (multispectral images, photos, and videos). [D; CSU] (Same as: AERO 108;GEOG 108;FTMA 108;NC 328)

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: ART OF HIEROGLYPHS
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
rows.description: Focuses on the principles of writing-system design, particularly Egyptian and Maya hieroglyphic writing, leading to an ability to understand the gist of the majority of Maya texts. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: INTRODUCTION TO DIGITAL IMAGING
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Recommended Concurrent Enrollment: ART 192L.
rows.description: Introduces digital imaging to graphic artists, artists, and photographers. Covers basic instruction on the digital image, Macintosh computers using Adobe Photoshop software, film and flatbed scanners, and archival printers. Emphasizes the application of technology for image optimization, enhancement, manipulation, composites, and collages. [D; CSU; UC; C-ID ARTS 250]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: INTRODUCTION TO DIGITAL IMAGING LABORATORY
requisites: Corequisite: ART 192.
rows.description: Allows digital imaging students to practice and review techniques and concepts introduced in Introduction to Digital Imaging. Provides an opportunity for the student to refine design, digital, and software skills beyond normal classroom time. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICES AND PORTFOLIO DEVELOPMENT FOR VISUAL ARTISTS
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
rows.description: Allows third-semester art majors to develop both a traditional and digital portfolio of their work. Includes contemporary issues in art research on career opportunities, galleries, art schools, methods of documentation, and resume writing. Includes visits to local museums and art galleries. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: PORTFOLIO DEVELOPMENT FOR VISUAL ARTISTS LABORATORY
requisites: Corequisite: ART 197.
rows.description: Allows visual art students to practice and review techniques and concepts introduced in the portfolio development course. Provides an opportunity for the student to refine portfolios beyond normal classroom time.

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: CONTEMPORARY ART PRACTICES SITE-SPECIFIC ART
rows.description: Introduces an in-depth study of new genres in contemporary art and examines the history and theory of installation and site-specific art, recent artistic practices, and technologies. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: OPEN STUDIO: THREE-DIMENSIONAL MEDIA LAB/NEW GENRE: INSTALLATION AND SITE-SPECIFIC ART
requisites: Corequisite: ART 200.
rows.description: Provides extended instruction, augmenting comprehension of the principles of art and design and the application of appropriate utilization of tools in the execution of installation and site-specific art. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: BEGINNING DIGITAL PHOTOGRAPHY
requisites: Recommended Concurrent Enrollment: ART 205L or ART 192.
rows.description: Introduces photographic theory, history, and cultural influences. Emphasizes the adjustable camera for effective visual communication and personal expression. Examines aesthetics, color theory, composition, content, and critical evaluation of student work. Includes basic instruction of image editing software for manipulating imagery. Appropriate for students without prior photographic experience. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: BEGINNING DIGITAL PHOTOGRAPHY LABORATORY
requisites: Corequisite: ART 192, ART 205, ART 206, ART 208A, or ART 212A (may be taken previously).
rows.description: Allows photography students to practice and review techniques and concepts introduced in Beginning Digital Photography. Provides an opportunity for the student to refine photographic skills beyond normal classroom time. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: INTERMEDIATE PHOTOGRAPHY
requisites: Recommended Concurrent Enrollment: ART 206L.
Prerequisite: ART 205 or ART 121 or equivalent.
rows.description: Focuses on creative assignments in a variety of photographic styles. Includes intermediate techniques of exposure control, high dynamic range, digital photographic aesthetics, digital workflow, medium and large format cameras, and electronic flash. Assignments are in color and grayscale. Requires an adjustable camera with manual exposure mode. A digital SLR is recommended. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: INTERMEDIATE PHOTOGRAPHY LABORATORY
requisites: Corequisite: ART 192, ART 205, ART 206, ART 208A, or ART 212A (may be taken previously).
rows.description: Allows photography students to practice and review techniques and concepts introduced in intermediate photography. Provides an opportunity for the student to refine photographic skills beyond normal classroom time. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: STUDIO AND LIGHTING TECHNIQUES
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 205 or ART 121 or equivalent.
Corequisite: ART 207L.
rows.description: Explores artificial lighting including strobes within the studio and the outside world. Emphasizes the control of light, quality of light, mixing natural and artificial light, basic portrait, and product lighting. Introduces techniques and concepts used in fine art and advertising photography. Requires an adjustable camera with a manual exposure mode. A digital SLR camera is recommended. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: STUDIO AND LIGHTING TECHNIQUES LABORATORY
requisites: Corequisite: ART 207.
rows.description: Allows photography students to practice and review techniques and concepts introduced in ART 207. Provides an opportunity for the student to refine photographic skills beyond normal classroom time. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: FILM AND DARKROOM PHOTOGRAPHY I
requisites: Recommended Concurrent Enrollment: ART 215A.
rows.description: Introduces the historical and technical aspects of film and darkroom photography with an emphasis on personal expression and visual literacy. Explores the historical, social, cultural, and personal significance of the photographic image in everyday life. Includes lectures and discussion on composition, content, light and exposure, film cameras, silver-based chemical processes, and presentation techniques. Requires an adjustable film camera. [D; CSU; UC]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: FILM AND DARKROOM PHOTOGRAPHY II
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 208A or equivalent.
rows.description: Refines basic film and darkroom skills learned in ART 208A, and emphasizes more complex creative silver-based photographic processes. Introduces an intermediate level of zone system exposure, medium format cameras, and large format cameras. Requires an adjustable film camera. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: FILM AND DARKROOM PHOTOGRAPHY III
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 208B or equivalent.
rows.description: Builds on basic film and darkroom skills learned in ART 208B, and emphasizes more complex creative silver-based photographic processes. Provides an intermediate-to-advanced level of zone system exposure, medium format cameras, and large format cameras. Requires an adjustable film camera. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: FILM AND DARKROOM PHOTOGRAPHY IV
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 208C or equivalent.
rows.description: Expands on basic film and darkroom skills learned in ART 208C, and emphasizes more complex creative silver-based photographic processes. Provides an advanced level of zone system exposure, medium format cameras, and large format cameras. Requires an adjustable film camera. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: PHOTOGRAPHY BUSINESS PRACTICES
requisites: Recommended Preparation: BUS 149 or equivalent.
rows.description: Emphasizes business related skills for a variety of photographic careers. Includes assisting, freelance, assignment production, studio work, photojournalism, stock photography, self-employment, and other photographic fields. Covers self-branding, organization, planning, client relations, legalities, pre-production work, budgeting, scheduling, and talent scouting. Requires participation in field trips, scenarios, and observing lectures by guest speakers. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: PORTRAIT PHOTOGRAPHY
requisites: Recommended Concurrent Enrollment: ART 210L.
Prerequisite: ART 207 or equivalent.
rows.description: Explores diverse aspects of portraiture including studio, headshots, environmental, and fashion photography. Introduces lighting and equipment specific to portraiture. Emphasizes styles, compositions, psychological considerations, and concepts associated with portraiture. Requires an adjustable camera with manual exposure mode. A digital SLR is recommended. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: PORTRAIT PHOTOGRAPHY LABORATORY
requisites: Corequisite: ART 210.
rows.description: Allows photography students to practice and review techniques and concepts introduced in Portrait Photography. Provides an opportunity for the student to refine photographic skills beyond normal classroom time. [D]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: EDITORIAL AND ADVERTISING PHOTOGRAPHY
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 207 or equivalent.
rows.description: Emphasizes the commercial application of photography. Discusses the relationship between photographer, art director, and client. Applies photography principles to magazine articles, advertisements, marketing, and promotion. Requires an adjustable digital camera with manual exposure mode and Camera RAW capabilities. A digital SLR is recommended. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: EDITORIAL AND ADVERTISING PHOTOGRAPHY LABORATORY
requisites: Corequisite: ART 211.
rows.description: Allows photography students to practice and review techniques and concepts introduced in ART 211: Editorial and Advertising Photography. Provides an opportunity for the student to refine photographic skills beyond normal classroom time. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: PHOTOGRAPHIC ALTERNATIVES I
requisites: Recommended Concurrent Enrollment: ART 215A.
rows.description: Explores alternative processes and techniques in photography. Emphasizes chemical-based processes including liquid emulsions such as cyanotypes and Liquid Light, as well as other techniques. Introduces alternative applications of technology in photography, including xerographic, digitally created negatives, and the merging of digital and chemical techniques. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: PHOTOGRAPHIC ALTERNATIVES II
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 212A or equivalent.
rows.description: Refines skills and concepts associated with alternative processes. Further explores liquid emulsions, alternative negative creation, and alternative cameras. Emphasizes aesthetics and conceptual issues relevant to non-traditional photography. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: PHOTOGRAPHIC ALTERNATIVES III
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 212B or equivalent.
rows.description: Develops skills and concepts associated with alternative processes at an intermediate-advanced level. Further explores liquid emulsions, alternative negative creation, and alternative cameras. Emphasizes aesthetics and conceptual issues relevant to non-traditional photography. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: PHOTOGRAPHIC ALTERNATIVES IV
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 212C or equivalent.
rows.description: Builds skills and concepts associated with alternative processes at an advanced level. Further explores liquid emulsions, alternative negative creation, and alternative cameras. Emphasizes aesthetics and conceptual issues relevant to non-traditional photography. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: SPECIAL TOPICS IN PHOTOGRAPHY
requisites: Recommended Concurrent Enrollment: ART 213L.
Prerequisite: ART 205 or ART 121 or equivalent.
rows.description: Provides additional exploration or photography through the examination of selected topics chosen from the following photographic genres: wedding, product, commercial, application of photography to industry, and the use of specific photographic techniques in fine arts. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: SPECIAL TOPICS IN PHOTOGRAPHY LABORATORY
requisites: Corequisite: ART 213, ART 192, or ART 205 (may be taken previously).
rows.description: Allows photography students to practice and review techniques and concepts introduced in ART 213: Special Topics In Photography. Provides an opportunity for the student to refine photographic skills beyond normal classroom time. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: PHOTOGRAPHY LABORATORY PRACTICE I
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 192 or ART 205 or equivalent.
rows.description: Allows photography students who have completed a beginning photography course to practice and review techniques and concepts introduced in photography-related classes. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: PHOTOGRAPHY LABORATORY PRACTICE II
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 214A or equivalent.
rows.description: Continues to allow photography and digital imaging students to practice and review techniques and concepts at an intermediate level. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: PHOTOGRAPHY LABORATORY PRACTICE III
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 214B or equivalent.
rows.description: Continues to allow photography students to practice and expand on techniques and concepts introduced in photography and digital imaging at an intermediate-to-advanced-level. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: PHOTOGRAPHY LABORATORY PRACTICE IV
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 214C or equivalent.
rows.description: Allows photography and digital imaging students the opportunity to practice and develop advanced techniques and concepts. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: DARKROOM PHOTOGRAPHY LABORATORY PRACTICE I
requisites: Corequisite: ART 208A or ART 212A (may be taken previously).
rows.description: Allows photography students to practice and review techniques and concepts introduced in photography related classes. Develops a photography portfolio for job application, transfer, or gallery exhibition purposes. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: DARKROOM PHOTOGRAPHY LABORATORY PRACTICE II
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 215A or equivalent.
rows.description: Allows photography students the opportunity to practice and review a combination of digital, film, and chemical-based photographic techniques and concepts introduced in photography related classes at an intermediate level. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: DARKROOM PHOTOGRAPHY LABORATORY PRACTICE III
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 215B or equivalent.
rows.description: Allows photography students the opportunity to practice and expand upon digital, film, and chemical-based darkroom techniques and concepts at an intermediate-to-advanced level. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: DARKROOM PHOTOGRAPHY LABORATORY PRACTICE IV
requisites: Prerequisite: ART 215C or equivalent.
rows.description: Allows photography students to practice and develop digital, film, and chemical-based darkroom techniques and concepts introduced in photography related classes. Develops a photography portfolio for job application, transfer, or gallery exhibition purposes. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: ADVANCED PHOTOGRAPHY
requisites: Recommended Concurrent Enrollment: ART 216L.
Prerequisite: ART 206 and ART 207, or equivalent.
rows.description: Emphasizes advanced problem solving in the photographic medium with the production of an individual student portfolio. Expands on concepts and techniques from beginning photography and intermediate photography. Requires an adjustable camera. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: ADVANCED PHOTOGRAPHY LABORATORY
requisites: Corequisite: ART 192, ART 205, or ART 216 (may be taken previously).
rows.description: Allows photography students to practice and review techniques and concepts introduced in advanced photography. Provides an opportunity for the student to refine photographic skills beyond normal classroom time. [D]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: DRONE AERIAL PHOTOGRAPHY AND CINEMATOGRAPHY
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Recommended Concurrent Enrollment: GEOG 107.
Prerequisite: ART 121 or ART 205 or FTMA 101 or equivalent.
Corequisite: GEOG 108 (may be taken previously).
rows.description: Provides beginning to intermediate uses of remotely operated vehicles for digital imaging, photography, and cinematography. Covers safety precautions, team collaboration, intelligent mission planning, common video movements, high resolution image capture, and editing. [D; CSU; UC] (Same as: FTMA 217)

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: WORK EXPERIENCE IN APPLIED ARTS I
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Recommended Concurrent Enrollment: Enrollment in one other class directly related to the Art major in order to apply learned theory in a practical hands-on setting through an internship class.
Prerequisite: ART 100, ART 159, ART 192, or ART 205, or equivalent.
Limitation on Enrollment: Declared Art major.
rows.description: Introduces principles and skills acquired in Art majors to on-the-job assignments. One unit of credit is granted for every 54 hours of work experience. Credit may be accrued at the rate of 2 to 4 units per semester for a maximum of fourteen units. The job supervisor and instructor will evaluate each student's job performance. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: WORK EXPERIENCE IN APPLIED ARTS II
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Recommended Concurrent Enrollment: Enrollment in one other class directly related to the Art major in order to apply learned theory in a practical hands-on setting through an internship class.
Prerequisite: ART 290 or equivalent.
Limitation on Enrollment: Declared Art major.
rows.description: Applies beginning-level principles and skills acquired in Art majors to on-the-job assignments. One unit of credit is granted for every 54 hours of work experience. Credit may be accrued at the rate of 2 to 4 units per semester for a maximum of fourteen units. The job supervisor and instructor will evaluate each student's job performance. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: WORK EXPERIENCE IN APPLIED ARTS III
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Recommended Concurrent Enrollment: Enrollment in one other class directly related to the Art major in order to apply learned theory in a practical hands-on setting through an internship class.
Prerequisite: ART 291 or equivalent.
Limitation on Enrollment: Declared Art major.
rows.description: Covers intermediate-level principles and skills acquired in Art majors to on-the-job assignments. One unit of credit is granted for every 54 hours of work experience. Credit may be accrued at the rate of 2 to 4 units per semester for a maximum of fourteen units. The job supervisor and instructor will evaluate each student's job performance. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: WORK EXPERIENCE IN APPLIED ARTS IV
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Recommended Concurrent Enrollment: Enrollment in one other class directly related to the Art major in order to apply learned theory in a practical hands-on setting through an internship class.
Prerequisite: ART 292 or equivalent.
Limitation on Enrollment: Declared Art major.
rows.description: Covers advanced-level principles and skills acquired in Art majors to on-the-job assignments. One unit of credit is granted for every 54 hours of work experience. Credit may be accrued at the rate of 2 to 4 units per semester for a maximum of fourteen units. The job supervisor and instructor will evaluate each student's job performance. [D; CSU]

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: INDEPENDENT STUDY
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Limitation on Enrollment: Eligibility for independent study.
rows.description: Individual study or research in some area of art of particular interest to the student and not included in regular courses of the college. [D; CSU; **UC] (**UC Limitation: credit for variable topics courses is given only after a review of the scope and content of the courses by the enrolling UC campus.)

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: DARKROOM AND DIGITAL PHOTOGRAPHY LAB
requisites: Corequisite: ART 121] Designed for photography students to practice and review darkroom techniques, camera usage, and exposure control.
rows.description: [ [D; CSU] (Formerly: ART 118)

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: ART HISTORY SURVEY---STONE AGE TO THE AGES OF FAITH
requisites: Recommended Preparation: RDG 158 or equivalent or through the Southwestern College multiple measures placement processes.
rows.description: Surveys the development of Western art in painting, sculpture, architecture, and handicrafts from prehistory through the medieval period. [D; CSU; UC; C-ID ARTH 110] (Same as: ARTH C1100)

rows.subject: ART
rows.title: ART HISTORY-RENAISSANCE TO CONTEMPORARY
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Recommended Preparation: RDG 158 or equivalent or through the Southwestern College multiple measures placement processes.
rows.description: Surveys a variety of artistic traditions and the history of visual cultural production from the Renaissance to present day. Analyzes the aesthetic and cultural development of painting, sculpture, architecture, and handicrafts. [D; CSU; UC; C-ID ARTH 120] (Same as: ARTH C1200)

rows.subject: ARTH
rows.title: SURVEY OF ART FROM PREHISTORY TO THE MEDIEVAL ERA
rows.description: This course introduces students to visual art and architecture from prehistory to the medieval era with a focus on art from Europe, North Africa, and the near East. The course will further consider global interactions involving these regions. [D; CSU; UC; C-ID ARTH 110] (Same as: ART 150)

rows.subject: ARTH
rows.title: SURVEY OF ART FROM THE RENAISSANCE TO CONTEMPORARY
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
rows.description: This course provides an overview of art and architecture from the Renaissance to the contemporary period with a focus on art from Europe. The course will further consider global interactions involving this region. [D; CSU; UC; C-ID ARTH 120] (Same as: ART 151)

rows.subject: ASIA
rows.title: ASIAN-AMERICAN HISTORY I
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Recommended Preparation: RDG 158 or equivalent or through the Southwestern College multiple measures placement processes.
rows.description: Covers the history of Asian Americans in the social, political, economic, and cultural development of the United States from the colonial era to the annexation of California in 1848. Emphasizes the Filipino, Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Asian-Indian, and Southeast Asian experiences. Includes study of the United States Constitution. [D; CSU; UC] (Same as: HIST 112)

rows.subject: ASIA
rows.title: ASIAN-AMERICAN HISTORY II
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Recommended Preparation: RDG 158 or equivalent or through the Southwestern College multiple measures placement processes.
rows.description: Examines the history of Asian Americans in the United States from 1846 to the present. Major themes include the study of economic developments, occupational patterns, anti-Asian movements, inter-ethnic exchanges, gender, and intergenerational issues. Includes a study of the Constitution of California. (Partially fulfills American Institutions requirement at CSU.) [D; CSU; UC] (Same as: HIST 113)

rows.subject: ASIA
rows.title: FILIPINO-AMERICAN HISTORY
rows.grading: Pass/No Pass or Grade is Allowed
requisites: Recommended Preparation: RDG 158 or equivalent or through the Southwestern College multiple measures placement processes.
rows.description: Emphasizes the economic, political, and social history of Filipinos in the Philippines and in the United States. Analyzes the effects of Spanish, American, and Japanese colonization on Filipino culture. Focuses on the major waves of migration to the United States and focuses on youth, intergenerational, women, gender, and political issues. [D; CSU; UC] (Same as: HIST 114)

rows.subject: ASIA
rows.title: FILIPINO-AMERICAN CULTURE
